clue.text: Mine repaired, reportedly with plenty of gold

parts.note: a mine and a well are both shafts sunk to extract something from the ground

indicators.note: reportedly means we take how a word for repaired sounds when spoken, not its spelling

parts.note: repaired means healed, as a wound mends

explanation.surface: A mine has been fixed up, and word is it holds a rich seam of gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' turns HEALED (repaired) into the sound-alike HEELED. The surface makes 'gold' part of the mine; it belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wealthy has plenty of money, and 'well-heeled' is the idiom for rich.

clue.text: Healthy pickles consumed by ladies no end

indicators.note: consumed by means the pickles word is swallowed inside the ladies word
no end means the last letter of the ladies word is dropped

parts.note: ladies are women
a pickle is a difficult spot, also called a hole

explanation.surface: Ladies devour a jar of pickles as a supposedly healthy snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pickles' reads as food, but a pickle is a fix or hole; 'no end' drops the last letter of the ladies word before it swallows the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Healthy and wholesome both describe food or habits that are good for you.

indicators.note: abandoning means the letter for North is left out of the families word

parts.note: families are lines of descent, as in a noble line

explanation.surface: Stories of families leaving the North behind for a new life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoning' takes N out of LINES (families, as in bloodlines).
explanation.definitionFit: Tales can mean falsehoods, as in 'telling tales', which are untruths.

clue.text: Famous man's high point, I see

parts.note: man's, as a possessive, means his
a tor is a rocky hilltop, a high point on a moor
see is the sound of the letter C

explanation.surface: A man points out his favourite summit and says he understands.
explanation.walkthrough: A TOR is a rocky hill on English moorland such as Dartmoor.
explanation.definitionFit: Something famous enough to be remembered in the record of the past is called historic.

indicators.note: consumed by means the answer is swallowed inside the run of letters Gareth ostentatiously

explanation.surface: Gareth shows off his team spirit with a lot of ostentation.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the join of 'GarETH OStentatiously'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethos is the characteristic spirit or guiding beliefs of a group.

parts.note: the emu is a large flightless Australian bird
LA and TE are two notes of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A songbird copies the notes it hears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' gives two sol-fa notes side by side, LA and TE.
explanation.definitionFit: To emulate someone is to copy them, matching or rivalling what they do.

clue.text: A knot that's tied with dearest in church, on impulse

indicators.note: in means the dearest word sits inside the church letters

parts.note: dearest is a term of endearment, like love
an itch is an urge or impulse to do something

explanation.surface: Two people tie the knot in church on a sudden romantic impulse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tied the knot' suggests a wedding; the knot here is a sailor's hitch. 'on' just places ITCH after C-LOVE-H.
explanation.definitionFit: A clove hitch is a common knot used to fasten a rope round a post.

clue.text: Buoyant one getting depressed without love

parts.note: one can be the article a

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the depressed word wraps round the love letter

parts.note: flat means low in spirits, depressed
love is zero in tennis scoring, written O

explanation.surface: Someone stays cheerful despite feeling low after losing their love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside, not lacking: FLAT goes round O.
explanation.definitionFit: Buoyant means floating, and something afloat is kept up on water.

clue.text: There's a possibility they'll go to the dogs

definitions.text: There's a possibility they'll go to the dogs

parts.words: There's a possibility they'll go to the dogs
parts.note: the idiom for ruin is read literally: scraps from a meal that may be fed to the family's pets

explanation.surface: Something faces a real chance of falling into ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go to the dogs' means decline, but here it means be given to the dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Uneaten food remaining after a meal is often handed to pets.

indicators.note: as they say means the residence word is spoken and a sound-alike is wanted

parts.note: a hall is a large country residence

explanation.surface: Someone is told to move a house, so the saying goes.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech the two words sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: To haul goods is to carry or transport them.

indicators.note: nameless means the letter for name, N, is taken out

parts.note: wild can mean violent, uncontrolled

explanation.surface: An unidentified wild flower is found in a hedgerow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' looks like it describes the flower but gives VIOLENT; N is a standard abbreviation for name.
explanation.definitionFit: The violet is a small purple spring bloom.

clue.text: Greek dish-or most of French dessert, otherwise

indicators.note: most of means the French dessert word loses its last letter

parts.note: mousse is a light French whipped pudding
aka, also known as, introduces another name, like otherwise

explanation.surface: A menu offers either a Greek dish or a large helping of French pudding instead.
explanation.walkthrough: AKA stands for 'also known as'; 'otherwise' does the same job, as in 'John, otherwise known as Jack'.
explanation.definitionFit: Moussaka is a baked Greek casserole of aubergine and minced lamb.

clue.text: An anti goes wild enough to alienate

indicators.note: going wild suggests the letters of an anti goes run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: A protester runs riot enough to drive people away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges AN ANTI GOES; 'enough to' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To antagonise people is to make them hostile, turning them against you.

clue.text: Glutton grabs time to prepare a snack

indicators.note: grabs means the glutton word takes hold of the other letters inside itself

parts.note: a hog is a greedy person, a glutton
to do food is to prepare or cook it

explanation.surface: A greedy eater seizes a moment to fix himself something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glutton' looks like the eater of the snack, but it is the container; 'prepare' gives DO as in doing a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A frankfurter in a bun is a classic fast-food bite.

clue.text: I'm cutting cloth with hint of tailor's smooth application

indicators.note: cutting means the I'm letters slice into the cloth word

parts.note: linen is a cloth woven from flax
taken as written, without the apostrophe

indicators.note: hint of means just the first letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: A tailor describes cutting cloth with a smooth finishing touch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' looks like tailoring, but it signals one piece slicing into another; the tailor only lends a first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A liniment is a soothing lotion rubbed onto aching muscles.

definitions.meaning: in grammar, a verb form for ongoing past action

explanation.definitionFit: It names a past verb form, and also means flawed or not in working condition.

parts.note: brass means cheek or impudence, also called sauce
mug and pan are both slang for the face

explanation.surface: A container made of brass, perhaps a drinking cup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brass' and 'sauce' are both British slang for cheek; 'mug' and 'pan' both mean face.
explanation.definitionFit: A pan with a handle used for cooking on a hob is a kitchen vessel.

parts.note: a check or bill in a bar is a tab

indicators.note: new means the letters of metal are made afresh in a different order

explanation.surface: A diner inspects a newly made metal item on the dinner table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Check' here is the American sense of a bill, as in picking up the tab; 'new' scrambles the five letters of 'metal'.
explanation.definitionFit: A protective mat placed under plates at dinner is a piece of tableware.

parts.note: a band is a group, of musicians or people
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A group finishes its business in good time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrap up' suggests finishing; here it is a noun for a dressing wound round an injury.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip of material wound round a wound is a covering wrap.

definitions.meaning: to emerge or flow out, as water from a source

explanation.definitionFit: It means a leap, and also to arise or flow forth, as a stream from the ground.

indicators.note: only half means just the first half of the explored word is kept

parts.note: explored means investigated, looked into

explanation.surface: A danger has been only partly looked into.
explanation.walkthrough: INVESTIGATED has twelve letters; 'only half' keeps the first six.
explanation.definitionFit: To hazard money is to risk it, as one does when putting it into shares.

definitions.meaning: read literally, a pick worked by hand

explanation.definitionFit: It means choose with care, and read in parts it describes a hand-operated digging implement.

parts.note: a suit is a lawsuit or petition, also a plea

indicators.note: original means the first letter of the trousers word

explanation.surface: A suit with trousers that still have their original crease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' looks like clothing but is a legal case, PLEA; 'original' takes T from 'trousers'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleat is a fold pressed into fabric, like a sharp crease.

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cape on maps
the raven is a large black bird of the crow family

explanation.surface: A bird from the Cape has yellow plumage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yellow' looks like a colour but means cowardly.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow is slang for cowardly, and craven means lacking courage.

clue.text: Dance round circle, forming a ring

indicators.note: round means the dance word goes round the circle letter

parts.note: a hop is an informal dance
a circle is shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Dancers move round in a circle, forming a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts O inside HOP.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoop is a circular band, such as a child's toy or a barrel's metal band.

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot on taps
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A powerful hot drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strong' looks like it describes the drink but is the definition, meaning healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Hale means robust and vigorous, especially of an older person.

clue.text: Declares old and feminine should be in bustles

indicators.note: in means the old and feminine letters go inside the bustles word

parts.note: to bustle or press on is to hurry forward

explanation.surface: Someone states that elderly, ladylike fashion calls for bustles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bustles' suggests Victorian skirts but is a verb, PRESSES, meaning hurries; 'should be in' puts O and F inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To profess a belief is to state it openly, to declare it.

parts.note: a reformist is read as one who re-forms things, as metal is heated and cast into a new shape in a crucible

explanation.definitionFit: A crucible where metals are liquefied and recast; figuratively, a society where cultures blend.
